title: Updated: Mountie charged in shooting death of ex-Flin Flonner
article: An RCMP officer has been charged with manslaughter in the fatal 2015 shooting of former Flin Flon area resident Steven Campbell in Thompson.
Cst. Abram Letkeman is alleged to have fired the bullets that claimed Campbell's life following a pursuit in the northern Manitoba city on Nov. 21, 2015.
dangerous driving causing bodily harm, and dangerous driving.
Letkeman has been with the RCMP for seven years and was stationed in Portage la Prairie at the time of his arrest, according to a police statement referenced by CBC.
The charges against Letkeman followed a lengthy investigation by the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU), which probes serious incidents involving police officers in the province.

Campbell, 39, was a father of two and former longtime resident of the Flin Flon area. The shooting also seriously injured a female passenger CBC identified as the mother of Campbell's daughter. Two other passengers were not injured.
There are differing accounts of the events leading up to the shooting.
Citing information from the RCMP, the IIU initially said an officer noticed an erratic driver and attempted to complete a traffic stop.

"After a brief pursuit, the vehicle was stopped and the officer approached it," read an IIU news release. "The vehicle then accelerated and struck the officer. The officer discharged his firearm. As a result, the male driver of the vehicle was pronounced deceased at the scene."
Campbell's mother, Shirley Huber, said a witness contradicted that account.
Shortly after the shooting, Huber said she spoke with a passenger who was in the vehicle in which Campbell was shot.
Huber said the passenger told her Campbell accelerated when the officer flashed his lights at them because he didn't want to get caught for impaired driving again.
The passenger, a female, told her the officer did not pull over Campbell's car but in fact slammed into it with a police vehicle, stopping it.

The officer then fired nine shots into Campbell's vehicle, striking him three times and a woman in the front passenger seat once, necessitating surgery to remove a bullet from her brain, Huber said she was told.
"The girl swore to me that she did not resist. They all had their hands up," said Huber, who lives in Alberta.
Last week, Shannon Heck, Campbell's sister, shared her thoughts with CBC.

"The officer is somebody who is supposed to be able to keep his calm and cool and for some reason or other he didn't do that and he didn't act appropriately," Heck said. "I don't think charging him with manslaughter is appropriate."
Letkeman has been released on bail with conditions to appear in provincial court in Thompson on March 31.
In a 2015 editorial, the Thompson Citizen argued Campbell's death gave the RCMP reason to consider using dash cams or body cams to record police interactions with the public.
